# SK2016 — A logger message is interpolated before it is logged

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A Microsoft.Extensions.Logging call receives an interpolated message instead of a stable message template.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Correctness |
| Default severity | suggestion |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 2.0 |
| Supersedes | CA2254 |

## Why

Interpolating before the logger sees the message eagerly renders values and discards their property names. A stable template preserves structured fields for filtering and aggregation and avoids rendering work when the log level is disabled.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
logger.LogInformation($"Loaded {count} items");
```

Write:

```csharp
logger.LogInformation("Loaded {Count} items", count);
```

## When it does not fire

The rule binds only calls to `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.LoggerExtensions` and only the argument bound to its `message` parameter. It does not guess from method names, custom logger types or unrelated interpolated arguments. No fix is offered because choosing useful property names and preserving format/alignment semantics requires author intent.
